summary: Lemma-free exact test (scripts/z52d_p2_TO0b_ff.py exists_general, cross-checked against the repo's Lemma 1.3 engine and data/ffl fail files, all identical) for A=T with leading coefficients of X,Y,Z in the squares H: q=5 (H={1,4}) n=2,3,4: monic fails 2,2,1 of 10,40,150 irreducibles, square-lc fails 0,0,0; q=7 (H={1,2,4}) n=2,3: monic fails 6,21 of 21,112, square-lc fails 0,0. All 10+40+21+112 square-lc witnesses were verified exactly (A XYZ = P(XY+YZ+XZ)). Free leading coefficients (all units): zero failures for q=3 (n<=5), 5 (n<=4), 7 (n<=3). So the index-2 cone already removes every monic failure in this range; the monic normalisation is what carries the hardness.
not_done: deg P = 8 not reached (n<=4 for q=5, n<=3 for q=7); q=3 squares are {1}, so monic; A = T only; no Z-side analogue checked.
next: Push q=5 to n=5,6 for square-lc and check whether any monic failure survives the index-2 cone at larger degree.

summary: Divisor closure is exact: if m/p = sum of k unit fractions and d | m then (m/d)/p = sum of k unit fractions (divide each denominator by d); checked with 0 violations for all censused numerators m in {1..10,12,16,25} and primes p<30000 (scripts/z52d_p2_TO0b_numer_closure.py; census data/z52b/pass2/TO0b/numer/). Hence ES(p) <=> 4 in M(p) <=> some multiple of 4 in M(p); in the census 4 is representable for all 3244 primes 5<=p<30000, so the first multiple of 4 is 4 itself and nothing new appears.
not_done: Only numerators m <= 25 censused (p < 30000); no test of M(p) beyond 25.
next: None from this item; the forced-numerator question is Z0108.

summary: Exact 3-term identities (1 + 1/((p+1)/2) + 1/(p(p+1)/2) = (p+2)/p and 1/1+1/(p+1)+1/(p(p+1)) = (p+1)/p) make m = p+1, p+2 and 2p+1 representable for all 301 primes 5..2000 (scripts/z52d_p2_TO0b_parity_numer.py); for p = 1 mod 4 none of these is 0 mod 4. Brute force over linear numerators m = a p + b (a in {1,2} since m/p <= 3) with 4 | m for all p = 1 mod 4 up to 2000: p+3 representable for 77/147, p-1 and 2p-2 for 1/147, 2p+2 for 0/147; no always-representable 0-mod-4 numerator (scripts/z52d_p2_TO0b_forced_linear.py).
not_done: Non-linear m(p) (e.g. m = (p^2+1)/k or m = 4k, k(p)) not tabulated; no check beyond p = 2000 for linear forms.
next: Test whether the 52% of primes with p+3 in M(p) (p = 1 mod 4) is a Chebotarev-type set (Q(sqrt(p+3))-type) or a congruence class mod 840.

summary: Divisor closure forces Fail(16) ⊇ Fail(8) ⊇ Fail(4) (verified: Fail(4) empty, Fail(8) = {3,11,17,131,241}, Fail(16) has 33 primes < 30000, Fail(8) subset Fail(16) holds). The hard-prime claim as stated is false for the ladder: 5, 13, 193 are in E_1 (8 in M(p)) but not in E_2 (16 not in M(p)), and 17 is in neither; for p = 5 the failure of 16 is trivially size (16/5 > 3). Census: m = 8, 12, 16, 25 representable for 99.85%, 99.35%, 98.98%, 97.53% of primes 5..30000.
not_done: Census only to p < 30000 and only numerators 8, 16 (not 32, 64); E_j defined as 'm*2^j in M(p)'.
next: Extend the census to p < 10^6 for m = 8, 16, 32 and check whether Fail(2^j) grows.

summary: Identity 4/n = 2/((n+1)/2) + 1/M + 1/M with M = n(n+1)/2 verified exactly for all odd n <= 10001. Note the first term is a numerator-2 fraction with denominator (n+1)/2, not a unit fraction, so this is a weighted identity, not a 3-term unit-fraction identity; the numerator-2 relaxation only changes the problem by one weight.
next: Only if weighted identities are pursued: classify weight vectors with uniform identities.

summary: Parity argument checked: for odd n, a sum of odd unit fractions equal to 4/n has an even number of terms (reduce mod 2 in Z_(2)); exhaustive search for 3-term odd solutions for odd n <= 301 gives none. Two odd unit fractions suffice for 969 of the 1500 odd n in [3,3001]; the first failures are n = 5, 7, 13, 17, 23, 25, 29, 31, 37, 41, 47, 49. The odd greedy termination problem itself was not attacked.
not_done: Odd greedy algorithm termination (not a finite check); 4-term odd representations for n <= 3001 not tabulated.
next: Tabulate the minimal even k (2 or 4) for odd n <= 3001 with a 4-term search.

summary: Parity forces an even number of odd unit fractions (checked: no 3-term odd solutions for odd n <= 301). Two odd terms suffice for 969 of 1500 odd n <= 3001 (test: 4/n = 1/x+1/y with x,y odd via divisors of n^2); the remaining 531 need k >= 4 (k = 4 not computed here).
not_done: k = 4 search (the item's second case) not run for the 531 failing n.
next: Run a 4-term odd search for the 531 failures with n <= 3001 (divisor-pair plus one free term).

summary: Representability census of m/p over all primes 5..30000 (scripts/z52d_p2_TO0b_numer_stats.py): all prime numerators 2,3,5,7 are representable for every p (exact trivial/known cases), composite 4 and 6 also for every p, while composite 8, 9, 10, 12, 16, 25 fail for 5, 3, 7, 21, 33, 80 primes respectively. So the split is prime-vs-composite only at m <= 7; the failure count is driven by the size of m, not primality.
not_done: Schinzel-table comparison at fixed n-range (the item's reference) not done; primes m >= 11 not censused.
next: Census m = 11, 13 to test whether primality helps beyond m <= 7.

summary: Exact bijection proved: 8/p = sum 1/x_i iff 4/p = sum 1/(2x_i), so 8-solutions correspond one-to-one to all-even 4-solutions. Checked for all 1611 primes p = 1 mod 4 below 30000: the number of 8-solutions equals the number of all-even 4-solutions (es census column 9) for every prime, and existence agrees (scripts/z52d_p2_TO0b_Z0212_bijection.py). The item's 'some denominator = 0 mod 4' variant is not tested as a bijection (it is not an identity).
not_done: Solution-by-solution map beyond counts (the explicit map is x -> 2x, which is exact); the 'some denominator div by 4' variant.
next: None; the coincidence is the identity 8-solutions = all-even 4-solutions.

summary: Exception sets for numerators m = 4, 9, 25 over all primes 5..30000 (census data/z52b/pass2/TO0b/numer): m = 4 fails for 0 primes, m = 9 fails for 3 primes (5, 11, 19), m = 25 fails for 80 primes (3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 29, 31, 41, ...), so odd prime squares do not behave like 4: 9 and 25 are strictly harder, and the failure count for m = p^2 grows fast with p. Representability of 25/p is 97.53% of primes (p=1 mod 4: 97.27%, p=3 mod 4: 97.80%), no residue-class split visible.
not_done: Exceptions for m=9,25 at n <= 10^5 and their 840-mod classes not analysed; the Mordell-type identity coverage modulo 840k not computed.
next: Compute which residue classes mod 840 contain the 80 exceptional primes of 25/p.

summary: Reduction checked: for l = 1 mod 8 the odd part (l^k+1)/2 is 1 mod 4 and a prime factor 3 mod 4 is what the unit mechanism needs. For all 44 primes l = 1 mod 8 below 1200 some odd k <= 5 works (k=1: 33 primes, k=3: 8, k=5: 3; scripts/z52d_p2_TO0b_unit_identities.py). No unconditional proof for all l was found: the 'no GRH needed' claim requires an Artin-type statement (a prime q = 3 mod 4 with v_2(ord_q l) = 1), which I did not establish.
not_done: Proof for all l; the l = 3,5,7 cases and primes l > 1200 not run.
next: Settle whether a prime q = 3 mod 4 with v_2(ord_q l) = 1 is known unconditionally (literature check: Murata/Moree on 2-parts of orders).

summary: Identity 4/n = 2/n + 1/n + 1/n checked exactly for all odd n <= 2001 (scripts/z52d_p2_TO0b_unit_identities.py). It is a numerator-relaxation identity with weights (2,1,1); it trivialises nothing by itself because 2/n is not a unit fraction.

In Z[1/2] the element 4 is a unit, so 4/p = 1/(p/4) is a one-term identity with p/4 in Z[1/2]; checked exactly for p = 5,7,11,13. The 'local-global' rewrite against STRONG_APPROX_ES.md was not checked.
next: Read STRONG_APPROX_ES.md for the reformulation and state the dyadic-place statement.

summary: Filter identity 4/p = 1/(p/3) + 1/(2p) + 1/(2p) verified exactly for all primes 5..400 (p/3 in Z[1/3], so one non-integral denominator). As a filter lemma: a 3-term S-integer representation with S = {3} always exists, so the S-integer relaxation with one non-integral denominator is trivial and carries no information about integer ES.
